category: observability: trace, event and metric store with a query engine

free_tier.stated: Free, 'free forever': up to 20M events per month and up to 100M metrics data points per month, 2 triggers, distributed tracing, BubbleUp, OpenTelemetry support, Honeycomb MCP; no credit card required
free_tier.notes: The allowance counts events and metrics data points, which no single unit of the vocabulary names. Each span of a trace counts as one event, so a trace of 150 spans is 150 events. Pro starts at USD 150 per month for up to 750M events.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: the event size limit is on the Events API page, which was not read

retention.stated: Events and logs: 60-day fixed retention. Time-series metrics datasets: 13-month fixed retention by default.

egress.terms: unverified: no egress term on the pages read; the Query Data API is listed among Enterprise features

interface_detail: Events and management API under /1/ and /2/ at https://api.honeycomb.io (US) or https://api.eu1.honeycomb.io (EU), keyed by API keys, plus OpenTelemetry ingest. The Query Data API is listed among Enterprise features. api.honeycomb.io answered 401 to /1/auth without a key.
tooling: OpenTelemetry SDKs and collectors, the Honeycomb MCP server, and any HTTP client with an API key
chaining: A trace and event store for free compute services instrumented with OpenTelemetry, 20M spans or events a month kept 60 days.

limits.value: 20M events per month (each span is one event) and 100M metrics data points per month
2000 events per second on the free tier; traffic above it gets HTTP 429

binding_note: Each span is one event, so a trace of 150 spans uses 150 of the 20M a month; the monthly event count binds before the 2000 events-per-second rate or the 60-day retention.

identity_cost.detail: Sign-up takes an e-mail address or a Google account, activated by a link sent to the e-mail, then a team name, a role and how the user heard of Honeycomb; the sign-up page states no credit card is required. The data region (US or EU) is chosen at sign-up. Whether a later step asks for a phone number is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: A team over its monthly event limit for a second consecutive month is warned, and after 10 days the Event API accepts one event in ten and rejects the rest.
confidence_note: Every limit is quoted from a first-party page, and the API host answered 401 without a key. No account was opened; an authenticated event send from a free team would move it to measured.
